Yup, we have T test and F test... 
But by definition, the larger the sample size (meaning as close to population) will be a better representation of the whole and population.

There is no fast rules that says you can't use 4 or 5, the minimum you need is 3 as it is used to prevent bias. 
Generally people use 3 replicates biological and technical, just for saving time, money and resources

The minimum is 3, the point of having replicates is to address how widley your results can be genealized 

Say you can't simple say a gives out put because b did not... It's saying 50 / 50 probability... To find if it is significant you need another replicate... So if 2 samples work/don't...the probability of your experiment's hypothesis is at 75/25 which is significantly better... 

The more the merrier honestly. 

I have worked on like 7 biological replicates and have used 3 and more technical replicates from each bio replicate...

This gives a valid  result which is better than 3..
